title: AI-Powered RF Signal Locator for Advanced Search and Rescue Operations
summary: MUST proposes machine-learning analysis of radio signals to locate people during search-and-rescue operations.
source_collection: ITU AI for Good: Innovate for Impact (2025)
account: The radio-frequency localization project is described as being in planning, with controlled-environment tests and field collaboration envisaged. It aims to improve search accuracy and speed. No completed rescue or measured operational improvement is reported.
purpose: Help rescuers locate people from mobile-device or beacon signals.
system: AI-Powered RF Signal Locator for Advanced Search and Rescue Operations

ratings.reason: The RF search-and-rescue proposal is explicitly in planning, with controlled tests described but no results.
No missing person is reported located or rescued through AI.

ai_role.statement: The account does not isolate AI’s contribution from the surrounding workflow.

evidence.citation: International Telecommunication Union, AI for Good: Innovate for Impact (2025). Project-submitted account, current as of June 2025. ITU provides no independent outcome evaluation.
evidence.title: Use Case 17: AI-Powered RF Signal Locator for Advanced Search and Rescue Operations

produced_by: The account does not establish conditions sufficient to reproduce the benefit.
must_hold: The account does not establish requirements for reproducing the benefit in other settings.

headline: AI-assisted radio localization aims to help search and rescue
claim_basis: Sources: the makers' report. The cited evidence includes no independent source and no finding by a regulator or court.
